facts.raw_span: A 25-year-old woman presented with a painless lump in the left cheek, first noted nine months earlier
no toothache, numbness, or systemic symptoms
no significant medical history
left facial asymmetry without skin changes
a firm, mobile, non-tender mass approximately 4 cm in diameter, located deep in the left buccal space and extending below the zygomatic arch
no cervical lymphadenopathy was noted
a bulge of the left buccal mucosa; palpation confirmed a well-defined, firm, non-tender mass
An orthopantomogram showed no bony destruction of the mandible or maxilla
Ultrasonography of the left cheek demonstrated a discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass measuring 2.6 × 2.0 cm, overlying the parotid gland
Contrast-enhanced CT of the head and neck revealed a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor measuring 2.7 × 3.7 × 4.0 cm in the left buccal space
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy yielded a hypocellular sample with erythrocytes, histiocytes, and neutrophils but showed “no signs of malignancy”
An intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated “wide fibroblast proliferation, extremely similar to a fibroma”

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a painless lump in the left cheek, combined with imaging findings of a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor and biopsy results showing wide fibroblast proliferation, is consistent with a fibroma.
The patient's imaging findings and biopsy results are consistent with a benign soft tissue tumor, which could include a fibroma or other types of non-malignant tumors.
The patient's presentation of a firm, mobile, non-tender mass in the left buccal space could be consistent with a lipoma, although the biopsy results did not specifically mention fatty tissue.
The patient's presentation of a firm, mobile, non-tender mass in the left buccal space could be consistent with a neurofibroma, although the biopsy results did not specifically mention nerve tissue.

The patient's lack of systemic symptoms and absence of cervical lymphadenopathy could be consistent with an inflammatory pseudotumor, although the biopsy results did not specifically mention inflammatory cells.
The patient's imaging findings could be consistent with a fibrosarcoma, although the biopsy results showed no signs of malignancy.
The patient's presentation of a firm, mobile, non-tender mass in the left buccal space could be consistent with a myofibroma, although the biopsy results did not specifically mention muscle tissue.
The patient's presentation of a firm, mobile, non-tender mass in the left buccal space could be consistent with a schwannoma, although the biopsy results did not specifically mention nerve tissue.

rationales.F05: The presence of a firm, mobile, non-tender mass is more typical of a benign tumor like fibroma.
rationales.F07: The bulge of the left buccal mucosa and the well-defined, firm, non-tender mass are consistent with a benign tumor.
rationales.F09: The ultrasonography findings of a discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass are consistent with a benign tumor.
rationales.F10: The CT scan findings of a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor are consistent with a benign tumor.
rationales.F11: The absence of signs of malignancy in the fine-needle aspiration biopsy makes fibrosarcoma less likely.
rationales.F12: The intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrating wide fibroblast proliferation is highly suggestive of fibroma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated wide fibroblast proliferation, extremely similar to a fibroma, and the imaging findings are consistent with a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor, which supports the diagnosis of fibroma.
